name: Paris
tagline: The café where the Revolution was sharpened, and the falafel with a line in Le Marais since 1979.

Le Cinq.description: Decor inspired by the Grand Trianon, inside the Four Seasons George V. Three Michelin stars.

Le Procope.description: Paris' oldest café, open since 1686. Voltaire, Diderot, and Rousseau all sat at its tables.

Le Baratin.description: Belleville bistro helmed by chef Raquel Carena since 1987. Anthony Bourdain's dinner here closed out his "No Reservations" Paris special, and it's a regular pick in the Le Fooding guide.

Virtus.description: Signature Franco-Brazilian cuisine in the 12th arrondissement. Two Michelin stars, new for 2026.

Guy Savoy.description: Classic French haute cuisine inside the Monnaie de Paris, on the banks of the Seine. Three Michelin stars.

Arpège.description: Alain Passard's vegetable-centric temple in the 7th arrondissement, sourced from his own Normandy gardens. Three Michelin stars since 1996.

L'Astrance.description: Pascal Barbot's tiny dining room in the 16th, with no fixed menu — the chef decides each day. Three Michelin stars.

Epicure.description: Éric Fréchon's restaurant inside the Le Bristol hotel, famous for its truffled lobster macaroni. Three Michelin stars.

Pierre Gagnaire.description: Avant-garde cooking served as multiple small compositions, from one of France's most influential chefs. Three Michelin stars.

Plénitude.description: Arnaud Donckele's restaurant inside the Cheval Blanc Paris hotel, overlooking the Seine from La Samaritaine. Three Michelin stars since 2021.

Kei.description: Kei Kobayashi's precise French-Japanese cooking near the Louvre. Three Michelin stars since 2020, the first Japanese chef to earn them in France.

Le Meurice Alain Ducasse.description: A gilded, Versailles-style dining room inside the Le Meurice hotel, under Alain Ducasse. Two Michelin stars.

Sur Mesure par Thierry Marx.description: Thierry Marx's all-white, technique-driven cooking inside the Mandarin Oriental Paris. Two Michelin stars.

Le Clarence.description: A former private mansion near the Champs-Élysées, backed by the Prats family's wine cellar (Château Lafite). Two Michelin stars.

L'Ambroisie.description: Classic haute cuisine in a former goldsmith's workshop on the Place des Vosges. Three Michelin stars since 1988, among the longest-held in Paris.

Alain Ducasse au Plaza Athénée.description: "Naturalness" cuisine built around fish, grains and vegetables, inside the landmark Avenue Montaigne hotel. Two Michelin stars.

David Toutain.description: Seasonal, vegetable-forward tasting menus from a former protégé of Bernard Loiseau and Alain Passard. Two Michelin stars.

Substance.description: Matthias Marc's small, minimalist dining room in the 16th, refined technique built on few ingredients. One Michelin star.

Yam'Tcha.description: Adeline Grattard's French-Chinese fusion, paired with tea instead of wine. One Michelin star near Les Halles.

Le Grand Véfour.description: An 18th-century dining room under the arcades of the Palais Royal, once frequented by Napoleon, Victor Hugo and Colette. One Michelin star.

Ze Kitchen Galerie.description: William Ledeuil's French-Asian cooking inside a former artist's studio in Saint-Germain-des-Prés. One Michelin star.

Benoit.description: A 1912 Paris bistro revived by Alain Ducasse, serving textbook bœuf bourguignon and cassoulet. One Michelin star.

La Tour d'Argent.description: An institution dating to 1582 across from Notre-Dame, famous for its numbered pressed duck (canard au sang), served since the 19th century.

Aux Lyonnais.description: An 1890 Lyonnaise bistro revived by Alain Ducasse, known for quenelles and saucisson chaud. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Septime.description: Bertrand Grébaut's bistro, ground zero for Paris's bistronomy movement since 2011, with a short market-driven menu and industrial-chic dining room.

Frenchie.description: Grégory Marchand opened this pocket-sized bistro on Rue du Nil in 2009 after stints with Jamie Oliver and Gramercy Tavern; Anthony Bourdain cited it as a marker of the new Paris bistro on "Parts Unknown".

Le Chateaubriand.description: Iñaki Aizpitarte's Belleville bistro, a global reference for the new bistronomy and a regular on the World's 50 Best list. Anthony Bourdain visited it on "No Reservations".

Clown Bar.description: A former bar of the Cirque d'Hiver, with its original Art Nouveau tilework, reborn as a natural-wine bistro built on quality produce.

Bistrot Paul Bert.description: A classic 11th-arrondissement bistro known for its benchmark entrecôte-frites and tarte Tatin; Anthony Bourdain visited it on "No Reservations".

Chez L'Ami Jean.description: A Basque-inflected bistro near the Eiffel Tower, loud and generous, famous for its riz au lait. Anthony Bourdain dined here.

Le Comptoir du Relais.description: Yves Camdeborde's bistro, credited as the birthplace of modern bistronomy, in the heart of Saint-Germain-des-Prés.

L'Ami Louis.description: A legendary bistro since 1924, famous for its roast chicken and duck-fat potatoes; a celebrity magnet for decades.

Josephine Chez Dumonet.description: A period-piece bistro in the 6th arrondissement, whose bœuf bourguignon Anthony Bourdain praised on "Parts Unknown".

Le Servan.description: The Levha sisters' bistro near the Place de la République, French cooking with Asian accents. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Le Dauphin.description: A marble room designed by Rem Koolhaas next door to Le Chateaubriand, serving French small plates alongside a strong natural-wine list.

Vivant Table.description: A 19th-century former bird shop turned natural-wine restaurant in the 10th arrondissement, its original tilework still intact.

Pierre Sang in Oberkampf.description: French-Korean chef Pierre Sang Boyer, discovered on France's "Top Chef" (2011), serves a no-menu surprise tasting at this walk-in-only Oberkampf spot.

Le Rigmarole.description: Yakitori grill and French-Asian cooking from a couple trained at Noma and Roberta's, in a tiny 11th-arrondissement room. One Michelin star.

Spring.description: American chef Daniel Rose's restaurant near the Louvre, a pioneer of no-choice single tasting menus in Paris.

Mokonuts.description: Moko Hirayama and Omar Koreitem's tiny spot, loved equally for its market lunch and its critically adored tahini cookies.

Chez Georges.description: A 1964 bistro near the old stock exchange, white tablecloths, steak tartare prepared tableside, and service unchanged for decades.

Allard.description: A 1931 Saint-Germain bistro, now under the Ducasse group, famous for its olive-braised duck and escargots.

Chez Denise (La Tour de Montlhéry).description: A Les Halles bistro open all night since the 1960s, checkered tablecloths and enormous portions of traditional cooking.

Auberge Pyrénées Cévennes.description: A Gascon-tradition bistro near the Place de la République since 1930, known for its cassoulet and duck dishes.

Robert et Louise.description: A meat-focused Marais bistro with a wood fire where the meat is grilled, unpretentious and unchanged since the 1960s.

Le Timbre.description: A tiny Montparnasse bistro run by a single chef at the open kitchen, praised by critics for its value.

La Régalade Saint-Honoré.description: A southwest-French tradition bistro near the Louvre, with the house terrine served table-side before the main course. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Au Pied de Cochon.description: A Les Halles brasserie open 24 hours since 1947, a survivor of the old central market, famous for its roasted pig's trotter.

Bofinger.description: An 1864 Alsatian brasserie near the Bastille, often called the oldest in Paris, famous for its Art Nouveau glass dome.

Brasserie Lipp.description: An 1880 brasserie on Boulevard Saint-Germain, a historic meeting point for writers and politicians, known for its choucroute.

La Coupole.description: A grand Art Déco Montparnasse brasserie opened in 1927, its columns painted by era artists, once frequented by Picasso and Man Ray.

Le Dôme.description: A Montparnasse seafood brasserie opened in 1898, a historic haunt of the international artistic bohemia.

La Closerie des Lilas.description: A Montparnasse brasserie where Hemingway wrote part of "The Sun Also Rises", brass plaques marking the seats of famous regulars.

Le Train Bleu.description: A Belle Époque restaurant from 1901 inside the Gare de Lyon, its painted ceilings protected as a historic monument.

Bouillon Chartier.description: A popular 1896 dining hall with original Art Nouveau decor, heir to Paris's old low-priced "bouillon" canteens.

Bouillon Pigalle.description: A modern revival of the popular "bouillon" canteen concept in Pigalle, traditional French cooking at very low prices, with a constant queue.

Bouillon Julien.description: A 1906 bouillon with one of the best-preserved Art Nouveau interiors in Paris, a listed historic monument.

Le Grand Colbert.description: An early-20th-century brasserie in the Galerie Vivienne, made internationally famous by a scene in the film "Something's Gotta Give" (2003).

Polidor.description: An 1845 crémerie-restaurant in the Latin Quarter, the setting for a scene in Woody Allen's "Midnight in Paris" (2011).

Café de Flore.description: An 1887 café in Saint-Germain-des-Prés, the literary headquarters of Sartre and Simone de Beauvoir in the 1940s.

Les Deux Magots.description: The Flore's rival café since 1884, once frequented by Hemingway, Picasso and André Breton, its terrace always full.

Angelina.description: A 1903 tea salon facing the Tuileries Garden, famous for its "L'Africain" hot chocolate and its chestnut Mont-Blanc pastry.

Ladurée Champs-Élysées.description: An 1862 pastry house credited with creating the modern double-shelled macaron, its Second Empire tearoom on the Champs-Élysées.

Pierre Hermé.description: The macaron and Ispahan boutique of the pastry chef the food press has dubbed "the Picasso of pastry".

Du Pain et des Idées.description: A 10th-arrondissement bakery run by Christophe Vasseur out of an 1875 shop, famous for its "pain des amis" and pistachio escargot pastry.

Poilâne.description: A family bakery since 1932 in Saint-Germain, famous for its large sourdough miche stamped with a "P", baked in a wood-fired oven.

Boulangerie Utopie.description: A modern 11th-arrondissement bakery widely praised by critics for its croissant and long-fermented traditional bread.

Chambelland.description: Paris's pioneering gluten-free bakery, using rice and buckwheat flour milled at its own mill in the Ardèche.

L'As du Fallafel.description: A falafel institution on the Rue des Rosiers since 1979, with a constant line in Le Marais. Anthony Bourdain recommended it on his show.

Chez Marianne.description: A Jewish deli and restaurant in Le Marais since the 1970s, serving mixed mezze plates to go or to eat in.

Mi-Va-Mi.description: A Marais falafel stand, the direct rival to L'As du Fallafel, with loyal neighborhood followers.

Sacha Finkelsztajn.description: The "Yellow Shop" of Le Marais, an Ashkenazi Jewish bakery and deli since 1946, famous for its strudel and pastrami.

Marché des Enfants Rouges.description: Paris's oldest covered market, opened in 1615 in Le Marais, lined with food stalls from around the world for eating on the spot.

Le Baron Rouge.description: A neighborhood wine bar next to the Marché d'Aligre, barrels for tables and oysters shucked curbside on weekends.

Septime La Cave.description: The natural-wine bar from Septime's owners, cheese and charcuterie boards to pair with glasses poured standing up.

Willi's Wine Bar.description: An Anglo-French wine bar opened in 1980 near the Palais Royal, a pioneer of the modern Paris wine-bar wave.

Frenchie Bar à Vin.description: Grégory Marchand's walk-in wine bar across from his restaurant Frenchie, charcuterie boards and natural wines by the glass.

Le Verre Volé.description: A wine shop and restaurant beside the Canal Saint-Martin, a pioneer of Paris's 2000s natural-wine scene.

L'Avant Comptoir.description: Yves Camdeborde's standing-only counter next to Le Comptoir du Relais, French tapas hanging from the ceiling and hand-carved ham.

Racines.description: A natural-wine bar tucked into the Passage des Panoramas, an early reference point for Paris's natural-wine movement.

Aux Deux Amis.description: An Oberkampf natural-wine bar with small-plate cooking, a regular meeting point for the 11th arrondissement's bistronomy scene.

Clamato.description: Septime's seafood-focused sibling on the same street, specializing in raw shellfish and shared plates, walk-in only.

Holybelly.description: A specialty-coffee shop that pioneered Australian-style brunch in Paris, near the Canal Saint-Martin, with a regular weekend line.

Ten Belles.description: One of the city's first single-origin roasters, beside the Canal Saint-Martin, a reference point for Paris's specialty-coffee wave.

Café Kitsuné.description: The coffee shop from the Japanese-French fashion brand, under the arcades of the Palais Royal, heavily photographed and viral on social media.

Berthillon.description: A family ice cream maker on the Île Saint-Louis since 1954, artisanal flavors and lines that wrap the block in summer.

Fromagerie Laurent Dubois.description: A 5th-arrondissement cheese shop run by a Meilleur Ouvrier de France, with in-house cave-aging and a selection of over 200 cheeses.

Barthélémy.description: A historic cheese shop on the Rue de Grenelle, a traditional supplier to the Élysée Palace for generations.

La Fromagerie Marie-Anne Cantin.description: An artisan cheese shop near the Eiffel Tower, raw-milk cheeses from small producers, aged in its own cave.

Breizh Café.description: A creperie that reinvented the Breton galette with seasonal ingredients and artisan cider, in Le Marais.

La Crêperie de Josselin.description: A classic Breton creperie in Montparnasse, a neighborhood long tied to Paris's Breton community.

Chez Omar.description: An unmarked Moroccan restaurant in Le Marais, famous since the 1980s for its couscous, with a loyal fashion-world following.

404.description: Mourad "Momo" Mazouz's Moroccan restaurant in a former Marais warehouse, a favorite of the fashion and celebrity crowd.

Le Petit Cambodge.description: A casual Cambodian restaurant in the 10th arrondissement, popular for its bo bun and soups, shared tables and a lively room.

Miznon.description: Israeli chef Eyal Shani's pita sandwiches in Le Marais, its whole roasted cauliflower gone viral on social media.

Terroir Parisien.description: Yannick Alléno's bistro dedicated to reviving recipes and produce from the Paris region, near the Place Maubert.

Au Petit Fer à Cheval.description: A Le Marais bistro since 1903, famous for its horseshoe-shaped bar.

Semilla.description: A Saint-Germain bistro with market-driven cooking and an open kitchen, rooted in Camdeborde's bistronomy school.

Verjus.description: A restaurant and wine bar run by an American-led team near the Palais Royal, tasting menu and a strong natural-wine list.

Le Pantruche.description: A neighborhood bistro in Pigalle known for its benchmark Grand Marnier soufflé. Michelin Bib Gourmand.
